items.q: What are the three main immune layers Huberman outlines?
items.a: (1) **Physical barrier** — skin + mucus-lined openings; (2) **innate** rapid response (neutrophils, macrophages, NK cells, complement); (3) **adaptive** slower targeted response (B/T cells, antibodies, memory).

items.q: Why prefer nasal breathing for immunity?
items.a: **Mucus is a filter** that traps/kills pathogens; site-specific microbiomes differ by eye/mouth/nose/gut. "Whenever possible… you want to be **nasal breathing**, not breathing through your mouth." Also avoid touching eyes after surfaces.

items.q: What fermented-food dose supports mucosal defense?
items.a: **2–4 servings/day** of low-sugar fermented foods (sauerkraut, kimchi, natto) support mucosal microbiota and **reduce cytokine activity** — fewer cells "calling for help."

items.q: How does foot elevation help when you're sick?
items.a: During early infection, **glymphatic clearance** ramps. Elevate heels ~**12°** (pillows under feet, head below legs) for more **glymphatic washout** during sleep.

items.q: What is the cyclic hyperventilation protocol at first symptoms?
items.a: **25–30 deep mouth breaths** → exhale hold **15–60 s** → **2–4 rounds** (often framed as 3×25–30). PNAS endotoxin study: ↑ **IL-10**, ↓ TNF-α/IL-6/IL-8, fewer flu-like symptoms via epinephrine — "zero-cost tool" bridging nervous and immune systems.

items.q: Why do people get sick on vacation?
items.a: Sustained adrenaline during crunch → **crash on rest** → illness emerges. The breathing tool **mimics short-term immune boost** from the same stress system used for psychological and pathogen combat.

items.q: How does hope affect immune recovery?
items.a: Ayssa Rolls lab: sense of **positive future/hope** → mesolimbic **dopamine** → anti-inflammatory cytokine shift (tumor size, wound healing). "A sense of hope is a sense of the future… tightly associated with the **dopamine system**."

items.q: What does electroacupuncture do for inflammation?
items.a: Qiufu Ma lab: hind-limb **electroacupuncture** → ProkR2 fascia neurons → medulla → adrenal catecholamines → **reduced inflammation**.

items.q: What dose of spirulina helps rhinitis?
items.a: **2 grams/day** (not milligrams) — double-blind RCTs (65–129 subjects) improved smell, sleep, work; reduced nasal itching/obstruction — alternative to dehydrating, sleep-disrupting OTC decongestants.
